plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Gain magnitude and lag/time-to-settle at mid-power, which set basic controller gain and integral time and determine what equilibrium and hold-input to test next.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with heat loss is correct, y rises monotonically from ~0.24 after a short lag with slowing slope, reaching roughly 0.4-0.55 by 180 s; flat trace would falsify gain, no decay of slope would suggest longer settling than one hold.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Decay behavior at u=0 and dominant time constant/ambient level, which sets heat-loss estimate, settling time, and feedforward hold input for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with heat loss is right, y decays monotonically from ~0.51 toward ~0.23-0.30 with slowing negative slope over 480 s, ending near ambient with slope near zero and +/-0.015 noise; flat or rising trace would falsify H1/H4.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Low-amplitude gain, dead-zone, and second point for linearity plus near-settled equilibrium to estimate hold-input for 0.5, which sets feedforward and controller gain.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with heat loss is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.16 after ~30s lag toward ~0.32-0.42 by 480 s with slowing slope to near zero; flat trace near 0.16 would falsify H1/H3, continued steep rise at end would imply larger gain/longer tau than E1-E2 suggest.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state gain/linearity at target level and hold-input for y=0.5, which sets feedforward and controller bias; discriminates H5/H6 by testing predicted 0.38->0.5 equilibrium versus higher/lower or nonlinear alternatives.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order with K~0.9, tau~150-200s and ambient~0.15 is right, y rises from ~0.37 toward ~0.49-0.51, reaching ~0.44-0.47 after 200s with positive but slowing slope (~0.0005-0.001/s) and +/-0.02 noise; flat or falling trace would falsify H1/H3, rapid jump above 0.55 would imply much larger gain.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state equilibrium and hold-input precision for y=0.5: extending the same 0.38 command to settling separates tau residual from true equilibrium and tests H5/H6 linearity prediction.
experiments.expected_observation: If first-order K~0.9 tau~100-160s ambient~0.15 is right, y holds 0.48-0.52 starting from ~0.49 with slowly decaying slope from ~0.0007 to ~0 and +/-0.02 noise, mean ~0.49-0.51; flat settling confirms hold-input ~0.39, continued climb above 0.55 or fall below 0.45 would falsify H5/H6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state hold-input precision for y=0.5 and residual tau: tests whether 0.33-0.35 holds target versus 0.38 high, which sets feedforward bias and integral need.
experiments.expected_observation: If first-order K~0.9-1.0 tau~120-200s is right, y eases down/up from ~0.535 toward ~0.48-0.51 over 150s with small negative-to-flat slope decaying to ~0 and +/-0.02 noise; settling near 0.50 confirms hold ~0.33-0.36, continued rise above 0.56 or fall below 0.45 would falsify H5/H6.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Residual time constant and true equilibrium at u=0.33 to pin hold-input for y=0.5, which sets feedforward bias and integral time.
experiments.expected_observation: If first-order K~0.9-1.0 tau~150-250s is right, y eases down from ~0.52 toward ~0.49-0.51 over 150s with slope decaying from ~-0.0005 toward ~0 and +/-0.015 noise; flat hold near 0.52 would imply y_ss(0.33)~0.52 and K~1.1, fall below 0.48 would imply lower equilibrium and hold-input above 0.33.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Delay and u=0 decay rate/equilibrium on changed machine to separate weaker actuator (similar decay, lower rise) from faster outflow (faster decay to lower ambient) and from slower response (longer flat delay), which sets new tau, hold-input bias and integral need.
experiments.expected_observation: If reduced-gain / increased-loss with near-original delay is right, y holds ~0.38-0.40 for ~20-30 s (still responding to prior ~0.57 in-transit commands) then falls monotonically toward ~0.12-0.20 over 300-400 s with initial fall slope ~0.0005-0.0015/s and +/-0.015 noise; flat hold near 0.39 for >100 s would imply much larger delay/tau, much faster fall to <0.15 within ~150 s would imply faster outflow, immediate rise would falsify gain/loss change.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Distinguish reduced heater power (C1) from increased heat loss (C2) via initial rise slope from near-ambient and new quasi-equilibrium; initial slope isolates P/C while plateau isolates K, which sets new feedforward hold-input for 0.5 and controller gain and rules out large-delay (C3).
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker actuator with near-original delay/tau is right, y holds ~0.13-0.16 for ~20-30 s (delay) then rises with reduced initial slope ~0.001-0.0015/s to ~0.25-0.33 by 200 s with slowing slope and +/-0.015 noise. If faster outflow is right, initial slope from near-ambient stays near-original ~0.002-0.003/s but plateaus lower ~0.25-0.30 quickly; flat >80 s would imply large delay, immediate jump >0.5 would falsify gain loss.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: New steady-state gain and equilibrium y_ss(0.5) / hold-input for 0.5, which sets new feedforward and whether target is reachable without saturation and discriminates reduced-gain plateau ~0.33-0.37 from faster-loss early plateau.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker actuator with near-original tau/delay is right, y rises from ~0.28 toward ~0.33-0.38 over 180s with slowing slope from ~0.0007 toward ~0.0002 and +/-0.015 noise, not yet fully settled. If faster outflow is right, y plateaus quickly ~0.27-0.30 with slope ->0; flat >80s then jump would imply large delay, rapid rise above 0.45 would falsify gain loss.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: New steady-state gain K_new and hold-input for y=0.5 / reachability of target, which sets revised feedforward bias and controller gain and confirms 0.5 is still reachable without saturation.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker actuator with K_new~0.45-0.55, ambient~0.13-0.14 and tau~130-200s is right, y rises from ~0.35 toward y_ss(0.8)~0.49-0.58 with initial slope ~0.0010-0.0018/s, reaching ~0.42-0.48 by 100s with slowing slope and +/-0.015 noise. Rapid jump above 0.60 or flat hold near 0.35 would falsify gain-loss; immediate fall would imply sensor/large-delay alternative.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive heater gain).
Original step response has small initial lag ~20-30s plus dominant tau ~150-200s, settling in ~400-600s.
No large dead zone: u=0.23 produces clear rise from ~0.15 to ~0.36.
At u=0 y decays on its own toward room ambient near 0.10-0.16; E2 fell 0.534 to 0.157 over 480s, E8 fell 0.351 to 0.136 over 480s, E9 starts ~0.13.
Original steady-state y is approximately linear in u with K~0.9-1.1 (y_ss ~0.13+K*u).
Original steady-state input to hold y=0.5 is ~0.32-0.34, likely ~0.33.
Original sensor noise is small ~0.005-0.01 rms, peak-to-peak ~0.013-0.03, smaller than 0.025 half-band; E8/E9/E10 noise similar apart from isolated dropouts.

Changed machine has weaker actuator (reduced K): same u holds lower y and step-up produces smaller rise; E9 u=0.5 from ~0.13 rose only to 0.28 in 200s with initial slope ~0.001-0.0015 vs original ~0.002-0.003, and E9+E10 380s at 0.5 only reaches ~0.35 vs original ~0.52, while E8 decay/ambient similar to E2 suggesting tau/delay near-original.

Changed machine has faster outflow / increased heat loss: E8 normalized decay similar to E2 and ambient ~0.135 similar to original, and E9 initial slope from near-ambient is much lower than original, contradicting preserved initial slope predicted by higher loss alone.
Changed machine has substantially slower response (larger delay/tau): E8 at u=0 fell immediately with no 30-40s flat hold and E9 started rising within ~10-20s, contradicting large delay.

Changed sensor (offset/bias or changed noise) explains low readings: E8/E9 noise ~0.01 similar to before and E9/E10 show sustained real positive slope under u=0.5, so pure offset or noise change cannot explain missing rise.
New steady-state gain roughly halved to K_new~0.4-0.55, so y_ss(0.5)~0.33-0.40 and input to hold y=0.5 is ~0.65-0.85 and y_ss(1.0)~0.55-0.68 remains above target.
